title: Live storm updates: Tornado Warning issued for Santa Cruz Co., reports of waterspouts on SF Bay
text:
Live Bay Area storm updates: Tornado Warning issued for Santa Cruz County, waterspouts spotted on San Francisco Bay - ABC7 San Francisco 
 24/7 Live San Francisco East Bay South Bay Peninsula North Bay Live WEATHER 
 Live storm updates: Tornado Warning issued for Santa Cruz Co., reports of waterspouts on SF Bay 
 By ABC7 Bay Area Digital Staff Last updated: Monday, November 16, 2026 9:08PM GMT 
 Stream local breaking news and original programming, live 24/7, from ABC7 Bay Area. A series of storms will bring heavy rain, flash flooding, gusty winds and possible debris flows to the San Francisco Bay Area over the next week.
 According to ABC7 Eyewitness News meteorologist Drew Tuma, this is a strong Level 2 storm on the ABC7 Exclusive Storm Impact Scale and could be bumped up to a Level 3 as it nears the region.
 LIVE: Track rain in San Francisco Bay Area with Live Doppler 7 
 In a forecast briefing released before 4 a.m. Monday, the weather service projected that the next system is expected to arrive Tuesday night and continue into early Friday morning, with the greatest impacts forecast for Wednesday and Thursday. Rain could linger across the region through the weekend.
 Moderate to heavy rainfall could cause minor flooding, while areas affected by recent wildfires face a higher risk of flash flooding, mud and debris flows. Some roads could become impassable because of flooding or damage, forecasters warned.

 Here's how the news is developing. 3 minutes ago 
 Reports of waterspouts over the San Francisco Bay 
 There have been sightings of waterspouts over the San Francisco Bay Monday afternoon.
 In several photos and videos circulating on social media, tall waterspouts can be seen going high up in the clouds.
 One was seen over San Francisco and others were seen on the Bay.
 This comes as a Tornado Warning was issued for parts of Santa Cruz County.
 21 minutes ago 
 Tornado Warning issued for Santa Cruz County 
 The National Weather Service has issued a Tornado Warning in Santa Cruz County on Monday afternoon.
 The NWS says that the warning is in effect until 1 p.m.
 Elsewhere, there have been reports of waterspouts on the San Francisco Bay.
 By Cornell Barnard 36 minutes ago 
 First responders urge safety as Bay Area beaches get battered by high surf 
 A powerful storm system is bringing rain, gusty winds and dangerous ocean conditions back to the Bay Area. A powerful storm system is bringing rain, gusty winds and dangerous ocean conditions back to the Bay Area, with officials warning the public to stay away from beaches as large swells move into the region.
 At Rodeo Beach in Marin County on Sunday, towering waves and thick seafoam drew spectators eager to witness the dramatic surf.
 "It's fun to come out and check it out. We don't see this every day," said Corte Madera resident Shannon Symmes.
 Craig Ross, who also traveled to Rodeo Beach, said seeing waves of that size was a rare experience.
 "To see waves like this once in a lifetime, or once every couple of years. Amazing," Ross said.
 Time-lapse video from the beach captured waves surging across large stretches of sand as the swell intensified.
 In nearby Bolinas, rough surf battered the community boat ramp. Christian Anthony of West Marin Feed described the force of the ocean as high tides combined with the incoming swell.
 "Just a ton of energy, a ton of power. All exacerbated by high tide," Anthony said.
 The powerful surf was causing damage elsewhere along the coast as well. In Mendocino County, high tides and heavy waves left the Arena Cove parking lot in Point Arena strewn with rocks and debris, forcing its closure.
 Farther south, video from Carmel-by-the-Sea showed waves estimated at about 30 feet crashing along the shoreline.
 With another round of large swells expected this week, first responders are urging people to admire the ocean from a safe distance.
 "We're telling people to stay away from beaches. Don't even come out. It's fun to see but stay away. It's for your safety," said Capt. Ian Hanson of the Southern Marin Fire District. "Watch it on the news, Instagram or YouTube. Just wait for things to settle before you go to the beach."
 Forecasters say hazardous coastal conditions are expected to continue through the week as stormy weather, high tides and powerful waves combine to create dangerous conditions along Northern California's coastline.
 By Karina Nova 36 minutes ago 
 Dangerous surf hammers Pacifica coastline Saturday 
 Massive waves could be seen all along the coast from Rockaway Beach in Pacifica to the pier, people showed up to see the wrath of the ocean on Saturday. Massive waves could be seen all along the coast from Rockaway Beach in Pacifica to the pier, people showed up to see the wrath of the ocean on Saturday.
 "It's Saturday. A beautiful day and it's pretty epic, go down to mavericks you can see the crazies riding these things," said Drew Edling from San Diego.
 The waves arrived with a High Surf Warning.
 "Very humbling, that was pretty crazy, that's for one thing you don't want to do," one man said. "That was insane, I'm sopping wet!"
 In one Pacifica neighborhood, flooding kept residents busy.
 "This was the worst we've seen it. It was up to knee high earlier, it's terrible."
 People worked nonstop to help prevent damage to their property.
 "We spent the last 4 hours filling sand bags...we're going to reward ourselves with some tacos."
 Despite the circumstances, neighbors tried to stay in good spirits, while working together.
 And for anyone who needs a reminder, you don't have to be grown up to know, you don't want to mess with mother nature.
 "I wouldn't come out here and everyone be safe," said Zoey, Pacifica resident. "Be careful out here guys, it's crazy!"
